newsitem.title: USA: Vermont Yankee nuke restart delayed to next week.
newsitem.headline: Vermont Yankee nuke restart delayed to next week.

text.p: Vermont Yankee Atomic Power Co said Thursday it postponed the restart of its 510 megawatt (MW) nuclear power plant in Vernon, Vt., to next week after automatically tripping off line a week ago.
"We're aiming at coming on line middle of next week, probably Wednesday (but) could be sooner or later," said a spokesman at the plant.
The operator originally planned to return the plant to service by the end of the week.
The spokesman said engineers found evidence of overheating of components inside the plant's main transformer.
"We've ordered parts and will be installing them in the next couple of days," he said.
The Vermont Yankee station was shut while engineers were performing instrumentation work and triggered an electronic signal that tripped the plant.
The facility stayed down to repair leakage at the reactor's main steam isolation valves and to correct an oil leak in the plant's transformer.
Central Vermont Public Service is majority owner of Vermont Yankee.
